title: FG% and FT% Anchors and Liabilities
brief: Which players move our team FG% and FT% most, up or down, given their shot volume? It must note that percentages are team ratios driven by attempts and that FT% is the least stable category year to year.
summary: FG% and FT% are team ratios, so a player's effect depends on his attempts as much as his percentage. A 41% shooter on 19 shots a game hurts you far more than a 59% free throw shooter on 3 attempts. Pick one percentage category to lean into rather than chasing both. Treat FT% as the shakiest projection of the nine categories, and never assume a percentage lead is safe in a low-volume week.

sections.heading: Attempts decide how much a shooter matters

paragraphs.text: In our league, FG% and FT% are team totals for the week: all makes divided by all attempts. A player who takes many shots moves that ratio a lot. A player who takes few barely moves it. Good efficiency on low volume does not matter much. When you rank shooters before the auction, read attempts per game next to the percentage. Never read the percentage alone.

Shooting categories are rate stats with no floor. A high-volume bad shooter in your daily lineup keeps dragging the ratio down every night he plays. You can lose a category lead on the last day of a matchup. Check your FG% and FT% margins before the final day of each week. If a lead is narrow and you do not need a poor shooter's counting stats, consider benching him that day.

sections.heading: FT% is the least stable category

paragraphs.text: Regress every shooting percentage in your projections. Year to year, two-point percentage correlates at 0.53, true shooting at 0.52, free throw percentage at 0.49 and three-point percentage at 0.45. Free throw percentage is now the least stable standard fantasy category. On draft day, do not pay extra for one season of unusually good free throw shooting. Do not write a player off for one bad season either.

Free throw swings in either direction usually do not last. They drift back toward the player's norm, and you cannot predict them. A hot or cold free throw start in the first weeks is not, by itself, a reason to trade for or away a player before the 2027-03-04 deadline. Compare it with his usual level first.

Describe a poor shooter by how he shot last season, not as a fixed fact. Only extreme cases are near certain. The notes name Giannis at the free throw line, projected at about 64% on over 10 attempts a game. That is high volume at a low rate, so a team built on him should plan to punt FT% rather than hope he improves.

The notes do not disagree, but they look at different time frames. One note says free throw percentage varies most from year to year. Field goal percentage varies most from game to game and week to week. So FT% is the shakiest category when you draft. FG% is the one more likely to swing in any single head-to-head week.

sections.heading: Lean into one percentage, not both

paragraphs.text: Being strong in both FG% and FT% is very hard. If you only barely win both, the edge is fragile, and the money you spend on it leaves you short in other categories. In our 200 USD auction, choose a side early. One option is high-volume FG% anchors, usually bigs, with a weak FT% you accept. The other is high-volume FT% guards and wings, with a weaker FG% you accept. Then stop paying for the category you have given up.

When you pass on a player because of his shooting, check his volume first. A poor free throw shooter on about 3 attempts a game does little damage. A poor field goal shooter on 17 to 20 attempts can sink the category on his own.

Percentage categories are not safe in low-volume weeks. With fewer attempts, each miss moves the percentage more, so results swing more. Watch for weeks when your roster plays few games or injured players cut your attempts. In those weeks, do not count a percentage category as a sure win. Use your 6 weekly adds on categories you can control instead.

This matters most in playoff weeks 19, 20 and 21, which end Sunday 2027-03-28. A season-long FG% or FT% edge does not guarantee one playoff week. Check each player's games in those weeks. Keep the last-day rule in mind, because a single bad shooting night can flip a close ratio.
